Ibn Mas'ud and Abu Huraira explain verses of an-Najm about what the Prophet saw as Gabriel, whom he saw in his true form with six hundred wings.
Ibn Abbas says the Prophet saw his Lord with his heart; Aisha calls claiming he saw Him a lie, saying he saw Gabriel; Abu Dharr was told: Light.
Allah does not sleep, nor does it befit Him; He lowers and raises the scale, deeds are raised to Him by night and day, and His veil is light.
In Paradise only the mantle of grandeur over His face screens the Lord; He will lift the veil, and seeing Him will be dearer to its people than any gift.
Believers will see their Lord on Resurrection Day as clearly as sun and moon; each people follows what it worshipped, a bridge spans Hell, and many leave the Fire.
Those burnt in the Fire for their sins who hold a mustard grain of faith are brought out through intercession, cast into the river of life, and sprout like seeds.
The last man out of the Fire and into Paradise keeps asking for more and is granted the world ten times over; Moses asked about Paradise's lowest and highest ranks.
The hypocrites lose their light on the bridge over Hell, and by intercession people leave the Fire for Paradise; Jabir's account turned Yazid al-Faqir from the Khawarij view.
On the Day people seek intercession from Adam, Noah, Abraham, Moses and Jesus, who send them to Muhammad; he prostrates, intercedes in stages, and is first at Paradise's gate.
Every prophet has one prayer that is granted; the Prophet reserved his for interceding for his Ummah on the Day of Resurrection, for those who die associating nothing with Allah.
The Prophet recited Abraham's and Jesus's words about their people, raised his hands weeping for his Ummah, and Allah sent Gabriel to say He would please him regarding it.
Asked by a man where his father was, the Prophet said in the Fire, then called him back and said both his own father and the man's are there.
When 'Warn your nearest kindred' was revealed, the Prophet called Quraysh's clans and his family, warning he could not avail them against Allah; Abu Lahab retorted, and his surah followed.
Through the Prophet, Abu Talib, who defended him, will be in the shallowest part of the Fire, in shoes of fire that boil his brain, its lightest punishment.
Ibn Jud'an's keeping ties and feeding the poor will not avail him, the Prophet told Aisha, because he never said: My Lord, pardon my sins on the Day of Resurrection.
The Prophet declared openly that a certain family among his forefathers' descendants are not his friends; his friends are Allah and the pious believers.
Seventy thousand of the Ummah will enter Paradise without reckoning, faces like the full moon, using no charms, omens or cautery but trusting their Lord; Ukkasha is one of them.
The Prophet hoped his Ummah would be half the people of Paradise, though few as a white hair on a black ox, Gog and Magog being the Fire's thousands.
Cleanliness is half of faith, praising Allah fills the scale, prayer is light, charity proof, endurance brightness, and the Quran a proof for or against you.
No prayer is accepted without ablution, nor charity from pilfered war spoils; one in a state of impurity has no prayer accepted until he performs ablution.
Uthman showed the Prophet's ablution, washing each part three times and wiping the head, and reported that ablution done well, followed by prayer or walking to the mosque, expiates sins.
The five prayers, Friday to Friday, and Ramadan to Ramadan expiate the sins between them, so long as major sins are avoided.
Ablution done well with two attentive rak'ahs assures Paradise, and testifying after ablution that there is no god but Allah and Muhammad is His Messenger opens Paradise's eight gates.
Abdullah b. Zaid demonstrated the Prophet's ablution: rinsing mouth and nose, washing face and arms to the elbows, wiping the head front to back, and washing the feet.
In ablution water is snuffed into the nose and the nose cleaned, three times on waking as the devil spends the night there; cleaning with pebbles uses an odd number.
Seeing unwashed heels, the Prophet said woe to the heels from the Fire, ordering complete ablution; a man who missed a nail's breadth was sent back to redo it.
When a believer washes his face, hands and feet in ablution, the sins of each go out with the water, even from under his nails, until he emerges pure.
The Prophet's people will come shining on face, hands and feet from ablution, so he will know them, even those unborn, at his Cistern, where some will be turned away.
The Prophet speaks at the graveyard of people driven from his Cistern; a believer's adornment reaches where ablution reaches, and thorough ablution and waiting for prayer wipe out sins.
The Prophet would have ordered the tooth-stick at every prayer but for burdening people; he used it first on entering his house and on rising for night prayer.
Acts of fitra include circumcision, shaving pubes, cutting nails, plucking armpit hair and clipping the moustache, the last four within forty nights; the beard is grown to differ from polytheists.
The Prophet forbade facing the Qibla when relieving oneself, or wiping with the right hand, bone, dung or under three pebbles; Ibn Umar saw him with his back to it.
The Prophet loved starting from the right in ablution, combing and shoes; relieving oneself on paths or in shade invites cursing, and he cleansed himself with water Anas carried.
Jarir and Hudhaifa saw the Prophet urinate, once standing at a rubbish heap, then perform ablution and wipe over his socks; Hudhaifa disliked Abu Musa's extreme strictness over urine.
Mughira poured water as the Prophet, drawing his arms out under a tight gown, washed and wiped his forelock, turban and socks, which he had put on over clean feet.
Ali gives the limit for wiping over socks: three days and nights for a traveller, one for a resident; at the Conquest the Prophet prayed several prayers with one ablution.
On waking from sleep one must wash the hand three times before putting it in a vessel, for one does not know where it was during the night.
A vessel a dog licks is emptied and washed seven times, with sand or earth; the Prophet ordered dogs killed, then allowed dogs for hunting, herding and guarding crops.
None may urinate in standing water and wash in it, nor bathe in it when junub; the Prophet let a Bedouin finish urinating in the mosque, then had water poured.
When unweaned babies brought to the Prophet urinated on his lap or garment, he sprinkled water over it and did not wash it.
